rationale: A script over this app's BSB finds the word "leaven" in Matthew only at 13:33 and 16:6, 16:11 and 16:12, and the Greek noun is zyme in both places in the editions Bible Hub lists. At 13:33 "The kingdom of heaven is like leaven"; at 16:6 and 16:11 the disciples are told to "beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees," which 16:12 glosses as their "teaching." A word tracked within one Gospel is why the type is motif, following conn-gen3-seed-gen4-25 (a single recurring word) and conn-matt10-cross-matt16 (a recurrence within Matthew), and the verbatim recurrence of a word that occurs nowhere else in Matthew is why the label is strong. The row grades the recurrence, not a meaning: published readers explicitly set the two passages side by side but disagree about what follows. Calvin on 16:12 writes that at 13:33 "Christ had used the word in a good sense"; Meyer on 16:6 says leaven is "Used differently again in Matthew 13:33"; the Scofield Reference Notes read 13:33 through 16:11-12 and argue that leaven is "invariably used in a bad sense." That disagreement is reported in the lesson's Positions and in lesson 28's, unresolved.
